entities.summary: Andrzej Zebrzydowski, a Polish Roman Catholic bishop, played a crucial role in the religious landscape of 16th-century Eastern Europe. Born into a noble family, Zebrzydowski rose to prominence as a chaplain to Bona Sforza, the wife of Sigismund II Augustus, and later became a supporter of the king. His influence extended to the establishment of new bishoprics, including Kamieniec Podolski, Chełm, Włocławek, and Kraków. Zebrzydowski's legacy as a mediator between the Polish and Roman Catholic churches remains significant, especially in the context of the Protestant Reformation. His efforts to maintain Catholic orthodoxy in the face of growing Lutheran and Calvinist influences continue to fascinate historians. The impact of his chaplaincy to Bona Sforza, a member of the powerful Sforza family, highlights the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized the politics of the time. In 1560, Zebrzydowski died, leaving behind a complex and multifaceted legacy that continues to be studied by scholars today.
